messages.content:
You are a clinical validator checking whether a PTSD case
vignette accurately reflects a patient's required cognitive connections.

You will receive:
- A vignette to validate
- A list of REQUIRED edges that must appear
- A list of ACTIVE components that must appear

---

COMPONENT SYNONYMS
Each component may appear by its exact name or any accepted synonym:
  Triggers            → "triggers", "reminders", "cues", "triggering stimuli"
  Negative Appraisals → "negative appraisals", "negative beliefs", "appraisals", "distorted beliefs"
  Memory              → "intrusive memory", "trauma memory", "traumatic memory", "the memory"
  Threat              → "sense of threat", "perceived threat", "threat", "feeling of danger"
  Maladaptive Strategies → "maladaptive strategies", "avoidance", "maladaptive coping", "safety behaviours"

---

CAUSAL STANDARD
A required edge A→B is SATISFIED if, within the same paragraph:
  - Both A and B (or their synonyms) appear, AND
  - The paragraph conveys — through any language — that A influences, drives, or leads to B.
This includes direct causal sentences, sequential structure, or connecting phrases
like "because of", "this meant", "so", "which led", "as a result", "consequently", "in turn".
A required edge is MISSING only if no paragraph conveys the A→B relationship at all.

---

SECTION 1 — COMPONENT CHECK
Active components (must appear in the vignette):
  - Maladaptive Strategies
  - Negative Appraisals
  - Threat
  - Triggers

Confirm each component appears as a described feature of the patient's presentation.
This is an internal check only — do NOT add component results to violations.

---

SECTION 2 — REQUIRED EDGES
  - Triggers → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Triggers → Negative Appraisals
  - Negative Appraisals → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Threat → Maladaptive Strategies
  - Threat → Triggers
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Negative Appraisals
  - Maladaptive Strategies → Triggers

For each edge, apply the causal standard above.
- If satisfied: do nothing — only failures are reported.
- If missing: add it to violations and explain in one sentence what causal relationship is absent.

Validate the following vignette against the cognitive graph.

Keanu is a 63-year-old man whose large, calloused hands speak to a lifetime spent in construction, yet his eyes hold a deep, unsettled weariness. He came to therapy six months after the death of his wife, Leilani, stating he felt “hollowed out” and couldn’t seem to get his feet back under him. The story that unfolded was not one of simple grief, but of a trauma that had been walled off for decades. For twenty years, the woman he loved had also been his tormentor. Leilani’s abuse was unpredictable and private, a storm that could gather from a clear sky. It was her hands he remembered most vividly—one moment gentle as they served him dinner, the next clenched and cruel. He was a big man, strong enough to lift steel beams, but he had never once raised a hand back to her. This fact, once a point of pride, had curdled into a source of profound shame.

His life since her passing has been governed by a pervasive sense of threat. On the job site, the sudden shriek of a circular saw or the percussive bang of a nail gun will cause him to flinch violently, a jolt of pure adrenaline that leaves him trembling. This constant state of being startled and on edge makes him scan his environment relentlessly, a habit that sharpens his eye for potential triggers. Because he is always hypervigilant, he finds his gaze drawn to the very things he wishes to avoid; the way a female cashier’s rings catch the light, the specific shade of red on a stranger’s nails, or the sharp, bird-like angle of a woman’s wrist. He also wakes multiple times a night, sitting bolt upright in the dark, his heart pounding as he listens for footsteps that will never again come down the hall. This constant feeling of being unsafe fuels his need to control his environment, compelling him to adopt rigid, protective behaviours. At the union hall or a local diner, he will not sit until he has found a table near an exit, his back firmly to the wall.

These encounters with triggers, whether a fleeting visual reminder or a direct question about his late wife from a well-meaning friend, invariably send him spiraling. When his son recently tried to talk about a fond memory of Leilani, Keanu felt a familiar, cold dread wash over him. The conversation immediately activated the belief that he is fundamentally weak, a man who couldn't protect himself. This surge of self-loathing then dictates his actions. He cut his son off, claiming he was too tired to talk, and retreated to his room—a stark avoidance of the conflict he felt brewing. He has come to believe he is incapable of navigating any disagreement, from a simple dispute with a subcontractor at work to a heartfelt conversation with his own family.

This pattern of avoidance has become a suffocating feedback loop. The more he avoids conflict to manage his distress, the more evidence he gathers for his own inadequacy. After backing down from a younger foreman over a clear safety violation, he spent the rest of the day consumed by the thought, "I can't rely on myself to do the right thing." This corrosive belief that he is weak and unreliable directly feeds his impulse to retreat further. He has stopped going to family gatherings entirely, knowing his sister-in-law, who looks so much like Leilani, will be there. The strategy of avoidance, meant to protect him, only serves to isolate him and intensify the very triggers he is trying to escape, as his concerned son now calls more often, trying to breach the wall Keanu has built. His compulsive spending is another escape; when the feeling of being "dead inside" becomes unbearable, he finds himself online, buying expensive tools he doesn't need, chasing a momentary flicker of control that quickly dissolves into the shame of a mounting credit card bill, further proof of his unreliability. He finally sought help after his son, his voice tight with frustration and hurt, accused him of erasing Leilani’s memory. Keanu couldn’t explain that he wasn’t erasing her, but that he was drowning in the memory of her, and the last thing he felt he could rely on was himself.
